title: Folate

review.note: Drafted from the source below; not yet reviewed by a medical professional.

measures: A vitamin B test measures the amount of a B vitamin in the blood or urine. Folate (also called folic acid, or vitamin B9) helps the body make healthy new cells, and it is often measured together with vitamin B12.
context: The meaning of a vitamin B result is not always clear, because inflammation and some medicines can affect it, and labs use different ranges. Diets low in foods rich in B vitamins and conditions such as celiac or Crohn's disease can affect how well the body absorbs folate.
aboveRange: Large amounts of B vitamins can be associated with an underlying condition, such as some liver conditions
belowRange: Lower levels can be associated with certain types of anemia
May be associated with not getting enough folate from food or with trouble absorbing it
nextStep: Discuss this result with your doctor.
